text.p: SARAJEVO, May 6 (REUTER) - These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Ruling Moslem Party of Democratic Action (SDA) withdraws invitation to opposition Liberal Bosniak Organisation (LBO) to join a coalition for municipal elections after LBO president Muhamed Filipovic said his party does not want to help renew one-party monopoly.

- The biggest opposition party in Bosnia, Social Democratic Party (SDP), does not want to join the coalition led by the ruling SDA because it believes it can get at least eight percent of the vote on its own, says SDP president Zlatko Lagumdzija.
- Croat mayor of Mostar Ivan Prskalo and his Moslem deputy Safet Orucevic say tensions have eased in the divided town and report improvement in freedom of movement.
- Bosnia's Council of Ministers convenes in Croatian port of Dubrovnik to adopt a quick-start package needed for holding of the international donors conference for reconstruction of Bosnia.
- Bosnian people will never enjoy human rights until they learn to live together again, says human rights ombudsman for Bosnia Gret Haller.

- Moslem chairman of Bosnia's collective presidency Alija Izetbegovic meets delegation of Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) and expresses his hope that upcoming local elections will be better organised then general elections held last year. -- Sarajevo newsroom +387-71-663-864
